The '''European Congress of Mathematics''' ('''ECM''') is the second largest international conference of the [[mathematics]] community, after the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|International Congresses of Mathematicians]] (ICM).<ref>{{Cite web|title=EMS Congresses {{!}} European Mathematical Society|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/ems-congresses-0|access-date=2021-04-24|website=euro-math-soc.eu|archive-date=2021-08-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210801103820/https://euro-math-soc.eu/ems-congresses-0|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The ECM are held every four years and are timed precisely between the ICM. The ECM is held under the auspices of the [[European Mathematical Society]] (EMS), and was one of its earliest initiatives. It was founded by [[Max Karoubi]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=1st EUROPEAN CONGRESS OF MATHEMATICS|url=https://www.emis.de/ECM1.html|access-date=2021-04-24|website=www.emis.de}}</ref> and the first edition took place in Paris in 1992.

Its objectives are "to present various new aspects of pure and [[applied mathematics]] to a wide audience, to be a forum for discussion of the relationship between mathematics and society in Europe, and to enhance cooperation among mathematicians from all European countries".<ref>{{Cite web|title=European Congresses of Mathematics|url=https://www.emis.de/ECM.html|access-date=2021-04-24|website=www.emis.de}}</ref>

== Activities ==
The Congresses generally last a week and consist of plenary lectures, parallel (invited) lectures and several mini-symposia devoted to a particular subject, where participants can contribute with posters and short talks. Many editions featured also special lectures, e.g. by prize winners, and public sessions aimed at a general audience.

Other mathematics conferences and workshops organised in the same period become often satellite events of the ECM.

== Prizes ==
{{See also|European Mathematical Society#Prizes}}
Several prizes are awarded at the beginning of the Congress:<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prizes awarded by the European Mathematical Society {{!}} European Mathematical Society|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/prizes-awarded-european-mathematical-society|access-date=2021-04-24|website=euro-math-soc.eu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=History of prizes awarded at European Congresses of Mathematics {{!}} European Mathematical Society|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/history-prizes-awarded-european-congresses-mathematics|access-date=2021-04-24|website=euro-math-soc.eu|archive-date=2015-02-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150209183245/https://euro-math-soc.eu/history-prizes-awarded-european-congresses-mathematics|url-status=dead}}</ref>

* The '''EMS Prize''' (awarded since the first edition in 1992), to up to ten young mathematicians of European nationality or working in Europe
* The '''Felix Klein Prize''' (awarded since 2000), to at most three young applied mathematicians<ref>{{Cite web|title=Felix Klein Prize {{!}} European Mathematical Society|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/felix-klein-prize|access-date=2021-04-24|website=euro-math-soc.eu}}</ref>
* The '''Otto Neugebauer Prize''' (awarded since 2012) to a researcher in history of mathematics<ref>{{Cite web|title=Otto Neugebauer Prize {{!}} European Mathematical Society|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/otto-neugebauer-prize|access-date=2021-04-24|website=euro-math-soc.eu}}</ref>
*The '''EMS/ECMI Lánczos Prize for Mathematical Software''' (awarded since 2023), to a mathematician or scientist, or a group, for the development of outstanding [[mathematical software]] with important applications<ref>{{Cite web|title=EMS/ECMI Lánczos Prize {{!}} European Mathematical Society|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/ems-ecmi-lanczos-prize|access-date=2025-04-03|website=euro-math-soc.eu}}</ref>
*The '''Paul Lévy Prize in Probability Theory''' (awarded since 2023), to a scientist who has made outstanding contributions to [[Probability theory|Probability Theory]] and its Applications<ref>{{Cite web|title=Paul Lévy Prize {{!}} European Mathematical Society|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/paul-levy-prize|access-date=2025-04-03|website=euro-math-soc.eu}}</ref>
